content.text:
The preview lifecycle work (S9) is reviewed and committed, with its sign-off queued behind the MCP server change (S5). Neither is merged yet. Both features are now with workers.

**S9 (preview lifecycle):**
- One state machine tracks each preview run: absent, starting, running, stale, stopping, stopped.
- Effect now owns the child processes, port checks, signal handlers and cleanup.
- Readiness and stop waits use Effect's scheduling instead of sleep loops. The preview code now has no raw timers.
- A new start lock means two simultaneous starts end with exactly one owner.
- I removed one wrapper that passed a yes/no straight through the machine without deciding anything.
- I also rebased S9 onto S5, so its sign-off covers the exact tree it will merge as.
- One thing to watch: the launcher now returns an exit code instead of calling `process.exit`. The existing preview test will show whether the process still ends on its own.

**Sign-off queue, one at a time, each waiting for load below 6:** S5 first, then S9.

**Now running in parallel:**
- [S7 source-to-element](t3-thread://v2/63e16fdf-a1e1-4363-8349-45c9a3b50bc1/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A0fc5146e-3a24-492d-b871-e21a3331032d%3Adelegate-task%3A0c582ed3-41bf-4dea-92b8-d5c7f0730087):
  - Development builds tag each HTML element with the file and line that rendered it.
  - Selecting an element shows its source under Details, and comments and work requests carry it.
  - `civic elements <file>` works the other way, from a file or a diff to the elements it renders.
  - The first test runs on CIVIC's own screens.
- [S8 backend coverage](t3-thread://v2/63e16fdf-a1e1-4363-8349-45c9a3b50bc1/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A0fc5146e-3a24-492d-b871-e21a3331032d%3Adelegate-task%3Ab264f09d-7f42-4352-ac78-dc179f103a29):
  - The server routes and functions each journey reaches are worked out from the code and from recorded runs, never typed by hand.
  - There's a server section in the coverage panel and `civic coverage --backend`.
  - A test plants one deliberately unreached server function and checks that the report names it.

I'll add the MCP tools for both features myself once S5 lands.

I'm checking whether the `source` references would need changing too, and I also need to see whether the production flag ever gets set for builds, since the transform as written tags everything regardless of mode. The returned null source map could also cause small column drift in stack traces for tagged UI files, which I think is tolerable for now.

Production builds still get tagged because the transform never passes its production flag, and S7 overloads the existing `source` field with file locations, which is confusing. I'm checking how widely that field is used next.

content.text:
Source-to-element (S7) is reviewed, corrected and committed, but not merged. Its full sign-off, including the browser check on CIVIC's own screens, hasn't run.

**What S7 does:**
- In development, each HTML element in a project's own source gets the file, line and column that drew it. Production builds are never tagged, because the plugin only runs on the dev server.
- Selecting an element in the review overlay or on the canvas shows "Code location" under Details. Comments and work requests keep it, so the agent's work order names the file to open.
- `civic elements <file>[:<from>-<to>]` goes the other way, from a file or line range to the captured elements it renders. A helper turns a diff's changed lines into those ranges.

**What I changed:** S7 had stored the location in the field that already records where a record came from (which tool, which importer, which git line). That made the field's `line` mean two different things. It now has its own `location` field, with its own check that paths stay inside the repo.

**Test status:**
- Type checks and the lint baseline pass.
- The location and diff tests pass.
- The tagging test passes.
- The browser check on CIVIC's own screens, and the full suites, run in the sign-off.

**Load:** it has stayed at 8–9 for over half an hour. The cause is Orca's Playwright test runs in its own worktrees, not CIVIC. I'm keeping to the "below 6" rule, so the S5 sign-off, then S9, then S7, are queued behind it.

content.text:
Backend coverage (S8) came back unfinished. I've handed it to a new worker to complete; nothing new is merged.

**What the first worker built:**
- **Inventory:** CIVIC lists every server function a project defines, read from the code.
- **New hook for projects:** a project whose server has HTTP routes or RPCs can now report them to CIVIC as a generated list. This is a small, documented addition to what a project tells CIVIC.
- **Report:** recorded and replayed runs are turned into "which operations each journey reached". Only passing replays count; a replay that went wrong counts up to the step where it did.
- **Where you see it:** `civic coverage --backend`, and a new server section in the coverage panel.
- **What's missing:** the two examples with HTTP routes (Tasks and Team board) don't produce their route lists yet. Nothing was type-checked, linted or tested.

**What I did:** committed that work as a work-in-progress commit on its own branch. The new worker, [S8 finish backend coverage](t3-thread://v2/63e16fdf-a1e1-4363-8349-45c9a3b50bc1/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A0fc5146e-3a24-492d-b871-e21a3331032d%3Adelegate-task%3Ac02542bd-5e08-4552-b856-a191a28e7516), starts from it. It is to:
- read those route lists from the examples' own server code, never from a list typed into CIVIC;
- make the code pass type checks and the shrink-only lint baseline;
- run the browser test that plants one unreached operation and checks the report names exactly that one.

My checkout is back on the controller branch.

**Waiting to sign off, one at a time:**
1. The MCP server on Effect (S5)
2. The preview lifecycle (S9)
3. Source-to-element (S7)

The machine has stayed at about load 8 for over half an hour. Orca's test runs are the cause.

import path from 'node:path'
import { parseSync } from 'vite'

export const tagSources = (input, id, project, production = false) => {
  let code = input
  const file = id.split('?')[0]
  if (production || !/\.[jt]sx$/u.test(file) || !project.sources.some(root => file === root || file.startsWith(root + '/'))) return code
  const relative = path.relative(project.root, file)
  if (relative.startsWith('../')) return code

content.text:
Source-to-element (S7) failed its sign-off a second time and isn't merged yet. The fix for that failure is now in, and the browser check that failed passes.

**What went wrong:** the browser check found no tagged elements on CIVIC's own screens; the tags never reached the page. React's Vite plugin compiles JSX in an early step that runs before CIVIC's tagging step, and changing plugin order can't fix that because both run in the same early group. So the tagger never saw any JSX to tag. The worker hadn't been able to run this check, so this is the first time anything tested it.

**The fix:** tagging now happens when the file is read in, before any plugin compiles it, and only for files in the project's own source folders. I also removed the leftover "production" option, since the plugin only ever runs on the dev server.

**Verified:**
- The connector checks pass (66 of 66).
- The browser check on CIVIC's own screens passes: picking an element gives back the right file and line.
- The lint baseline is clean.

The full sign-off is running again. If it passes, I'll merge the feature together with the `elements` MCP tool. The worker finishing backend coverage (S8) is still running.

content.text:
Backend coverage (S8) works and its focused tests pass, but it's held back by 23 new lint findings, so it isn't merged.

**What S8 now does:**
- **Tasks and Team board:** both examples now handle their requests from route tables they define themselves (3 and 5 routes). CIVIC reads its list of routes from those same tables, so nobody keeps a second list by hand.
- **Reading list:** its server functions are found automatically from its code.
- **What counts as reached:** a route call only counts as reached by a journey if it succeeded; a response of 400 or above doesn't count. Routes with parameters, such as `/tasks/:id`, are matched properly.
- **For agents:** a `backend_coverage` MCP tool gives the same answer as `civic coverage --backend`, and a test checks the two match.

**Tests that passed:**
- Type checks
- The backend coverage and route tests (5)
- The runtime bridge tests (8)
- The browser record-and-replay flows for Tasks, Team board and Reading list

**What's holding it back:** 23 lint findings grew past the shrink-only baseline. They're mechanical: unchecked `!`, a missing regex flag, a shadowed name, `await` inside a loop. A new worker, [S8 lint cleanup](t3-thread://v2/63e16fdf-a1e1-4363-8349-45c9a3b50bc1/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A0fc5146e-3a24-492d-b871-e21a3331032d%3Adelegate-task%3A16209525-2cb7-42a2-8644-ba7b626bdb62), is fixing them in the code. It may not raise the baseline or switch rules off.

**Something the worker found, not yet checked by me:** replaying a recorded run that ticks a checkbox may compare against the wrong state. This was there before S8, and I'll look into it after these merges.

Source-to-element (S7) is still in its sign-off.

content.content:
## Implementation Units

### U1. Characterize journal and closure boundaries

**Goal:** Bind the existing recovery guarantees before changing resource ownership.
**Requirements:** R8–R10; AE4–AE7. **Dependencies:** None.
**Files:** `packages/canvas/server/runtime-service.check.mjs`, new `packages/canvas/server/runtime-lifecycle.check.mjs`, and small deterministic test fixtures under `packages/canvas/server/check-fixtures/`.
**Approach:** Extend the current backend fixtures with controlled worker and persistence barriers. Keep tests at actual journal and worker boundaries rather than duplicating internal state-machine logic.
**Execution note:** Add characterization coverage before modifying `runtime-service.mjs`.
**Test scenarios:**

1. Covers AE5. Drop a completed write response, close and restore, then resend the same intent and obtain the same receipt with one reconstructed write.
2. Covers AE6. Reopen a live run, send its previous owner's close lease and keep the replacement owner usable.
3. Covers AE7. Change source, seed or a replayed result and refuse restore while retaining the original journal.
4. Kill a fixture worker after intent persistence but before completion persistence; restore only completed entries and require explicit resend for the unfinished step.
5. Exercise existing account, reset, timezone and credential-redaction behavior across closure and restore.

**Verification:** Existing and new journal checks establish the R8–R10 baseline; no production behavior changes in this unit.

### U2. Add lifecycle decisions and scoped execution

**Goal:** Introduce one owner for host and run transitions without another durable store.
**Requirements:** R4, R5, R8–R10, R12. **Dependencies:** U1.
**Files:** New `packages/canvas/server/server-lifecycle.ts`, `packages/canvas/server/run-lifecycle.ts`, `packages/canvas/server/lifecycle.test.ts`, `packages/canvas/server/lifecycle-scope.test.ts`, `packages/canvas/tsconfig.server.json`; `packages/canvas/package.json`, `packages/canvas/vitest.config.ts` and `packages/pnpm-lock.yaml`.
**Approach:** Implement KTD2 and KTD5 with pure XState transitions and Effect-owned schedules. Serialize state changes with attach, expiry and stop events in the same owner queue. Keep host time independent of a run's synthetic clock.
**Test scenarios:**

1. Attach two clients, release either and remain serving; expire the final client and enter waiting.
2. Covers AE3. Reattach before the grace boundary and cancel that shutdown generation; an old timer or release cannot affect the replacement.
3. Run all deadlines under an injected clock, including startup with no client and no new work after stopping begins.
4. Interrupt a scoped task and verify finalizers settle once; a second stop request returns the same cleanup outcome.
5. Advance synthetic run time without changing real client expiry.

**Verification:** State and scope tests enforce KTD2, KTD5 and KTD7 deterministically without worker processes.

### U3. Supervise the existing run service

**Goal:** Give runs bounded, awaitable closure while preserving their public contract.
**Requirements:** R5, R8–R10, R13. **Dependencies:** U1, U2.
**Files:** `packages/canvas/server/runtime-service.mjs`, `packages/canvas/server/runtime-worker.mjs`, `packages/canvas/server/runtime-service.check.mjs`, `packages/canvas/server/runtime-lifecycle.check.mjs`; a scoped execution module if needed under `packages/canvas/server/`.
**Approach:** Keep validation and journal decisions in their existing owner. Place worker acquisition, listeners, expiry and per-run queues under scoped ownership. Add the stop fence before draining and cover pending spawn/restore paths. Retain the exported handle/close facade and existing limit values.
**Test scenarios:**

1. Covers AE4. Stop during a changing operation that finishes before the deadline and save its complete receipt before worker exit.
2. Stop during a hung operation, terminate within KTD5 and retain no false completion.
3. Race stop with worker creation and restore; no worker or successfully published envelope survives the closed scope.
4. Race duplicate resume, mutation and stale close events; preserve the single queue and R10 takeover behavior.
5. Fail journal persistence and worker startup separately; return failure, retain recoverable input and release resources.

**Verification:** U1's baseline and all existing runtime backends pass against the refactored service; real fixture workers exit without leaked handles.

### U4. Build managed discovery and authenticated presence

content.text:
Source-to-element (S7) passed its full sign-off at `648bdc39` and is merged into the controller branch, together with its `elements` MCP tool. The merged tree differs from the signed-off one only by the plan document.

**What's merged so far**

| Slice | What it is |
|---|---|
| S0 | The plan |
| S1 / S1b | Vite+ tooling and the dependency update |
| S2 | Lint checks against a recorded baseline that can only shrink |
| S3 | One install for all of CIVIC |
| S4 | The shared state-machine core and the work-request lifecycle |
| S5 | The MCP server on Effect |
| S6 | CIVIC as a project in its own picker |
| S7 | Source-to-element |
| S9 | The preview lifecycle |
| S9b | The cleanup helper for old preview builds |

**Running now**
- [S8 lint cleanup](t3-thread://v2/63e16fdf-a1e1-4363-8349-45c9a3b50bc1/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A0fc5146e-3a24-492d-b871-e21a3331032d%3Adelegate-task%3A16209525-2cb7-42a2-8644-ba7b626bdb62): the last 23 lint findings before backend coverage can be signed off.
- [S10 U1-U2 run journal tests and lifecycle machines](t3-thread://v2/63e16fdf-a1e1-4363-8349-45c9a3b50bc1/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A0fc5146e-3a24-492d-b871-e21a3331032d%3Adelegate-task%3A06c9b3d0-a7ce-47c7-b95b-7a786afc6dca): the first two of the app server's six units.
  - First it writes tests that lock in how recorded runs recover today.
  - Then it adds the app server and run state machines, with their timers tested on a test clock rather than real waits.
  - It doesn't wire them in yet.
  - One constraint I set: outside apps install the canvas package from git, so the new server-only dependencies must not become requirements for those apps.

**Next, once S8 merges**
- The agent-tool integrations (S11).
- The CIVIC ⇄ Orca hand-off tools (S11b): open a review for a worktree, link a request to a work item, read coverage.
- Checking the possible checkbox-replay mismatch the S8 worker found.

Bounded implementation worker for CIVIC (this checkout). Slice S11 "Harness integrations" of docs/plans/2026-11-15-effect-xstate-electron-rebuild.md (read §1 harness row, §6 S11, AGENTS.md, docs/decisions/0006 (CIVIC makes no model calls and launches no agents), 0007, 0022). Today: integrations/claude-code (Claude Code plugin: skills, hooks, bin/civic-mcp launcher, bin/civic-home, bin/session-start), integrations/claude-code/codex.mcp.json, root .claude-plugin/marketplace.json; the MCP server is review/src/mcp.ts (one Effect Schema tool table — TOOLS; do not edit its tools).

Goal: CIVIC is usable from any agent harness through the SAME stdio MCP server, with thin per-harness wrappers that only point at it — no per-harness tool lists anywhere (the server lists its own tools).
1. One launcher contract: `integrations/claude-code/bin/civic-mcp` (or a harness-neutral `bin/civic-mcp` it delegates to — choose the smallest) finds CIVIC's checkout (CIVIC_HOME) and starts the server. Harness configs reference only this launcher.
2. Config for each harness CIVIC documents, DERIVED from one small source (a single JSON/TS description of "command + args + env" rendered into each harness's config format by a function, with a test that every rendered config points at the same launcher): Claude Code (plugin, exists), Codex (codex.mcp.json / config.toml snippet), OpenCode (opencode.json `mcp` entry), Cursor (.cursor/mcp.json), and ACP agents (an ACP client passes `mcpServers` in `session/new` — document the stdio server entry; e.g. Amp, Gemini CLI via ACP). Do not write into the user's real harness config files; `civic integrate <harness>` (wired into review/src/cli.ts the way other commands are) PRINTS the snippet for that harness, and README explains where it goes. Lean on harness-native features (plugins/skills where the harness has them) but keep skills text harness-neutral.
3. Behaviour tests before any real agent (a "misbehaving agent" suite, real server process, temp git repo store, no mocks): drive the server exactly as a harness would over stdio (initialize → tools/list → calls) and assert refusals: a write with a stale `@version` is refused naming the change; claiming a request another agent holds is refused naming the holder; an agent cannot resolve (no resolve tool exists; any attempt via unknown tool name fails); report_fix without a claim is refused; oversized/invalid input is rejected naming the field. Also a smoke test per rendered config: spawn the launcher exactly as the config says (command/args/env) and complete initialize + tools/list.
4. New code lint-clean: `node bin/lint-baseline.mjs` must pass (shrink-only; CIVIC house style is fine).

Rules: never change HOME (set CIVIC_HOME/temp dirs via env in tests only); temp only in $TMPDIR; ephemeral ports only, never 3012 3013 4317 5733 4417 5734 10448 10449; never touch /Users/taymoor/Projects/CIVIC, any .civic-canvas folder, or any real harness config (~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.config/opencode, ~/.cursor); installs only inside this worktree (`pnpm --dir packages install --frozen-lockfile`); no new dependencies; no model calls. Load gate before any test suite: `bash /private/tmp/claude-501/REDACTED/8f3b2eca-0508-4f5d-8344-d9ed70c2da42/scratchpad/gate.sh`; ≤2 test workers. Do NOT commit, push, merge or delegate; leave changes uncommitted. Short why-only comments; README text in everyday words.

Verify: `pnpm --dir packages run check`, the new behaviour and smoke tests, `pnpm --dir packages --filter @civic/review test` after the gate. Report only: diff summary, the single source and the harnesses rendered, what each misbehaving-agent test asserts, commands with pass/fail, blockers.

content.text:
The agent-tool integrations (S11) are reviewed and committed. They aren't merged, and their tests haven't run yet.

**What S11 does:**
- Every agent tool reaches CIVIC through the same MCP server and its one launcher. The config for each tool is generated from a single description: Claude Code, Codex (JSON and TOML), OpenCode, Cursor, and ACP agents.
- `civic integrate <tool>` prints the snippet to paste. It writes nothing into your own agent settings.
- The server now refuses any text input over 64 KB, or 8 MB for images, and names the field.
- A test suite plays a badly behaved agent against the real server and checks that each of these is refused, with the reason named:
  - writing over a newer version;
  - taking someone else's claim;
  - trying to resolve a request;
  - reporting a fix without a claim;
  - sending bad or oversized input.

**Not yet run:** that suite, and the per-tool checks that start the launcher exactly as each config says. The machine never got quiet enough. The lint baseline passes, and so did the worker's type check.

**Sign-off queue, one at a time:**
1. S8, backend coverage (running or waiting now).
2. S10, the first app-server units.
3. S11, after a rebase onto S8, because both changed `mcp.ts`. The changes are in different places.

After those, the CIVIC ⇄ Orca hand-off tools (S11b) come next.
